_comment: Edit this file, not the code. Credentials never live here - they come from the SENEYE_USER / SENEYE_PWD environment variables.

site.title: Seagrass Nursery Monitoring
site.subtitle: Gibraltar Seagrass Restoration Project, North Mole

systems._comment: The five nursery systems. Each Seneye sits in a sump, and a sump serves the tanks listed against it.

devices._comment: Seneye device id -> the sump it monitors, read from GET /v1/devices on 21 Sept 2026. The system letter, tank list and label are looked up from the sump. If a unit is moved, change its sump here; readings already stored keep the mapping they were collected under.

parameters._comment: band = the nursery's own working range (shaded on the charts). hard = the range outside which a reading is flagged critical; null means no critical threshold set. Temperature, pH and NH3 are TNP set points supplied by Lewis Stagnetto, 21 Sept 2026. They are operating set points for this nursery, not published tolerances for Posidonia oceanica.

nh4.label: Ammonium (NH₄⁺, modelled)
nh4.model_note: Not measured. Worked out from the measured free ammonia, pH and temperature with the salinity in use, since NH3 and NH4+ are two sides of one equilibrium.

o2_sat.label: Oxygen at saturation (modelled)
o2_sat.model_note: Not a measurement of the oxygen in the tank. It is the most the water could hold at the measured temperature and the salinity in use, at sea-level pressure. Real dissolved oxygen sits below this whenever respiration outpaces exchange, and measuring it needs a probe.

slides._comment: Seneye slides last 30 days and are changed at the unit in the sump, so the countdown is per sump rather than per tank. Record the date a slide was changed as YYYY-MM-DD. 'default_changed' covers every sump, and an entry under 'changed' overrides it for that one sump. Changing a slide is a two-second edit here: add the sump and the date. When 'trust_sensor' is true and the Seneye reports its own expiry date, that is used instead and the dashboard says so; set it to false to go by the logged dates only. The dashboard works the days out in the browser, so the number counts down daily whether or not a harvest has run.

plugs._comment: Tuya smart plugs and the nursery air sensor, read only. The dashboard never switches anything: it is a static page on a public website, so it can hold no credential and a button on it would be a button anyone could press. Switching stays in the Smart Life app. Credentials live in the environment as TUYA_ACCESS_ID and TUYA_ACCESS_SECRET, never here. 'region' must match the data centre the Tuya cloud project was created in: 'eu' is Central Europe, 'weu' Western Europe, 'us' Western America. Each plug is a double, so each device has two sockets; which switch code drives which physical socket is not in the API, so confirm it with 'python tools/probe_plugs.py --toggle-test' before trusting the mapping. 'subscription_expires' is the expiry date of the project's IoT Core subscription on iot.tuya.com: Tuya stop answering when it lapses, which would leave the chiller column quietly frozen, so the dashboard says so once it is within 'subscription_warn_days' and every harvest warns in its log. Extend it on the platform and update the date here. 'stale_minutes' is for the plugs, which answer every poll, so silence means something is wrong. 'ambient_stale_hours' is for the air sensor, which is different: it reports when a value moves rather than on a timer, so a steady room legitimately sends nothing for hours. Judging it by the plugs' threshold made a healthy sensor look dead every time the nursery held still. Run the Air sensor reporting rate workflow to see what normal looks like for this sensor before changing it.

tariff._comment: Set 'per_kwh' to the nursery's electricity price and the dashboard shows a cost beside each row's consumption. Leave it null and only kilowatt-hours are shown. The figure is an estimate from half-hourly readings, so treat it as an indication of which row costs most to run rather than anything to put on a grant claim.

plugs.note: Chiller state is read from the plugs every harvest. It is shown here and switched from the Smart Life app.

devices._comment: 'sockets' maps a Tuya switch code to the sump its chiller serves. The socket order below is an assumption, lower-numbered sump on switch_1: run the toggle test and correct it if a plug turns out to be the other way round.

bf79a8d7fbe41cc23cdpxq.label: Nursery air
bf79a8d7fbe41cc23cdpxq._comment: Temperature and humidity of the air the tanks sit in, not of the water. 'scales' divides Tuya's scaled integers: their sensors report 213 for 21.3 degrees, so 10 for temperature. If the probe shows humidity as 655 rather than 65, set its scale to 10 as well. 'previous_ids' holds IDs this same physical sensor used before: a Tuya device that is factory reset, which rejoining it to a different Wi-Fi network will do, comes back with a brand new ID. Listing the old one here keeps its readings on the same chart instead of starting the record again from the day the router changed. Find the new ID with the Probe smart plugs workflow, ticking 'list every device'.

schedule._comment: The nursery chiller schedule, as designed in Chiller_schedule_2026. The dashboard does not run it: the plugs do, through Smart Life. What this block is for is checking that what the plugs actually did matches what was planned. Times are local to 'timezone' and a block whose 'to' is earlier than its 'from' runs over midnight. 'limits' is the cabinet constraint that the whole timetable exists to respect, one chiller running by day and three overnight, because each running DC2200 rejects about 2.95 kW into the enclosure. Editing a block here changes only what the dashboard expects to see, never what the plugs do, so a change made in Smart Life has to be made here too or the page will report a fault that is not one.

setpoints._comment: Chiller setpoints, a floor rather than the achieved temperature: the compressor starts 1 degree above setpoint and stops at it, so the time-average sits above by roughly half the drift.

nutrients._comment: In-situ samples taken by hand at the sumps, on different instruments from the Seneye probes. Read live from the Google Sheet on every run: paste the sheet's URL below, and in Sheets use File > Share > Publish to web > Nutrient > Comma-separated values so the harvester can read it without a login. Rows are matched to sumps by the Tank ID column (A12 -> SA12) and keyed on date + sump, so a corrected sheet overwrites the old values rather than duplicating them. If the fetch fails the stored samples are left untouched and data/nutrients.xlsx is used if present.
nutrients.method_note: In-situ spot samples: handheld meters and test kits, read by eye. Accuracy and resolution differ from the Seneye probes, so the two are shown as separate measurements and never averaged together.

derived._comment: Values the Seneye does not measure, calculated from ones it does. Salinity comes from the most recent in-situ sample for that sump; default_salinity is used only where a sump has no sample yet. Set nh3_as_nitrogen to true if your Seneye reports NH3 as nitrogen (NH3-N) rather than as ammonia. Equations and sources are in harvester/derived.py and the README.

insitu_reference._comment: Reference ranges for colouring the in-situ sample table. typical = ordinary local seawater (green). Between typical and outer is amber, meaning off typical but not alarming. Beyond outer is red. Derived from published seawater values for the western Mediterranean and Strait of Gibraltar and converted into the units this sheet uses; the workings and sources are in the README. These describe SEAWATER, not what Posidonia requires, and a red cell is a prompt to check the reading and the kit, not evidence of a problem. Calcium and magnesium are read in ppm and phosphate in ppb; in seawater 1 ppm is ~1.03 mg/L, so for calcium and magnesium the same numbers serve for both units and nothing is converted.

temp_c.basis: TNP nursery operating set points, not a seawater range

salinity_ppt.basis: Atlantic inflow ~36.2 to Mediterranean outflow ~38.4 at the Strait

ph.basis: surface ocean pH ~8.1; outer bounds are the nursery set points

no3.basis: western Mediterranean surface nitrate under ~4 umol/kg = 0.25 mg/L as NO3

no2.basis: upper-ocean nitrite 10-1000 nmol/L = up to ~0.046 mg/L as NO2

nh3.basis: surface ammonium typically under a few umol/L; check whether the kit reports total ammonia or free NH3

po4.basis: western Mediterranean surface phosphate ~0.16 umol/kg = 15 ppb as PO4; the sheet records ppb, so 0.05 ppm becomes 50 ppb

ca.basis: 412 ppm at S=35, scaling with salinity to ~452 ppm at S=38.4

mg.basis: 1290 ppm at S=35, scaling with salinity to ~1415 ppm at S=38.4

maintenance._comment: Issue tracking and planned jobs for anyone working at the nursery. Two tabs in the maintenance sheet: one row per fault, one row per recurring job. This log names people, so it is NOT published with the student dashboard: the board is written to board/ which the Pages workflow does not upload and .gitignore keeps out of the repo. Disabled for now: the maintenance log lives in Google until a private repo is available. Set enabled to true to start building the board, and publish to true only once you have decided that the log can be public, or set anonymise to true to strip names from the export.

issues._comment: gid is the number after gid= in the tab's URL. Publish this tab to the web as CSV the same way as the Nutrient tab.
